page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, tailored for environments demanding substantial memory capacity per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The physical configuration provides 2 physical cores supporting 2 threads per core, yielding 4 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware features 260 MB of L3 cache, along with Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction support. System memory totals 168.0 GB, establishing a high memory density of 42.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is provisioned without local disk storage and contains zero discrete GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the high clock speed of the Intel Xeon 8573C processor translates into strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2351.0, placing it in the top tier of evaluated machines, accompanied by strong single-threaded compression and decompression rates in gzip and bzip3. Conversely, multi-core metrics reflect the low core count, resulting in lower tier multi-threaded stress-ng results and an average Geekbench multi-core score of 5311.0. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register lower relative throughput, and larger language model inference tests demonstrate processing bottlenecks due to limited parallel compute.

The resource balance of the FX8-4ms_v2 presents clear cost-efficiency advantages for workloads that are priced on a per-core licensing model. By consolidating 168.0 GB of memory across just 4 vCPUs, organizations can reduce software licensing overhead while maintaining massive memory footprints. However, the absence of local storage requires external network-attached storage for persistent state. The instance aligns technically with in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, relational databases requiring substantial buffer pools, and single-thread-dominated data processing jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a memory-intensive, compute-focused virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs. The architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Equipped with 168.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an unusually high allocation of 42.0 GB per vCPU, though it includes no bundled local storage and no dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2351.0 and rapid single-threaded decompression rates, whereas multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth remain constrained due to the 4-vCPU limit. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-per-core ratio benefits workloads bound by commercial per-core software licensing fees. FX8-4ms_v2 is engineered for memory-heavy databases, in-memory caching systems, and single-thread-dominated analytical operations.
